summary: Gone Perry County lookout. A 1938 Forest Service plan approval is the only build record found; a communications tower stands on the site now.

facts.design: 80-foot steel tower, planned with a dwelling, garage, latrine and cistern
facts.status_note: Not standing; a communications tower and a small fenced building occupy the site, with one old footer visible
facts.agency: Hoosier National Forest, Lafayette district (now Tell City)

access.note: Public property just off old Indiana 37; no tower stands to climb

visit.trail_note: A Mogan Ridge area trail sign stands a few feet from the old tower site

events.note: Forest Service list records a plan approved January 28, 1938. The approval is for the plan; no source confirms the tower was completed.
Derby topo quad shows the tower just east of old IN-37. Map depiction only.
A 1997 trail map reproduced on Indiana Fire Towers shows a tower near the Mogan Ridge trails. Map depiction only.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Forest Lookouts names the Lafayette Unit of the Hoosier. The Forest Service calls the Lafayette district now Tell City. Both names refer to the same district, so the record's agency value stands.

sources.title: Lookout Towers
sources.publisher: USDA Forest Service, Hoosier National Forest

notes_for_editor: The only build record is the January 1938 plan approval on the Forest Service list. No source confirms construction, a builder, staffing, fires or removal date. The 80 ft plan height is converted to 24.4 m. The record's coordinates agree with the site author's GPS reading to about 0.0001 degree. The 1997 map is a depiction only, not proof the tower stood then. Agency name matches the Forest Service Lafayette district, now Tell City.
